skill_gaps_ranked: C/C++ for embedded/real-time flight software -- the #1 gap by a wide margin. Quantitative check today across 185 GNC/flight-controls/autonomy postings from 8 company boards (Anduril, Shield AI, Merlin Labs, Ursa Major, Apex, Slingshot Aerospace, Elroy Air) found C++ named explicitly in ~25% of listings, and it's an unstated assumption in nearly all flight-software/embedded roles. Resume lists Python/Java/HTML-CSS-JS, not C/C++.

Sensor fusion & state estimation (Kalman/EKF/UKF filtering) -- sensor fusion language appeared in ~76% of the same 185 postings (Shield AI's dedicated State Estimation ladder, Anduril's Navigation & Estimation track). Explicit Kalman-filter/state-estimation phrasing was rarer (~6%) but concentrated in exactly the senior GNC reqs this profile is a few years from qualifying for -- worth building toward now.

Flight test experience -- ~45% of the same postings mention flight test directly. The resume's HIL and motion-capture validation are lab-grade, not flight-line; several target companies (Anduril, Shield AI) have dedicated Flight Test Engineer tracks that could be a stepping-stone into GNC.

PX4/ArduPilot autopilot stack -- named explicitly by multiple air-vehicle startups found this week (Neros Technologies, Delta Black Aerospace, and previously Auterion, Skyways). Hands-on time with an open autopilot stack (vs. from-scratch MATLAB/Simulink work) is a recurring ask.

Rust -- an emerging requirement (~11% of postings, concentrated at Anduril and Shield AI's newer mission-autonomy and edge-systems roles). Not on the resume at all; lower priority than C++ but worth tracking as these companies scale.

DO-178C / safety-critical software certification -- ~17% of postings. Complements the resume's hardware/system safety background (MIL-STD-882E, FHA, FTA) but doesn't cover software certification standards specifically -- a natural extension given the Boeing Phantom Works system-safety internship.

Trajectory optimization tooling (GPOPS-II, CasADi, Dymos, IPOPT) -- a recurring Anduril preferred qualification; the resume's trajectory planning experience is closer to path/waypoint generation than numerical optimal-control tooling.
